title: Price Bands
statement:
Label every product with a price band so shoppers can filter the catalog.

The `products` table has one row per product:

- `id`: the product's id, unique
- `name`: the product's name
- `price`: its price in dollars, with cents

Return each product's `id`, `name`, `price`, and a `band` column, ordered by `id`. The band is:

- `cheap` when the price is under 20
- `standard` when the price is at least 20 and under 100
- `premium` when the price is 100 or more

Expected output:

```text
 id |        name         | price  |   band
----+---------------------+--------+----------
  1 | USB Cable           |   9.99 | cheap
  2 | Wireless Mouse      |  24.50 | standard
  3 | Mechanical Keyboard | 119.00 | premium
  4 | Laptop Stand        |  45.00 | standard
  5 | Phone Case          |  19.99 | cheap
  6 | Monitor             | 249.99 | premium
  7 | Webcam              |  79.00 | standard
(7 rows)
```

hints: `CASE WHEN condition THEN value ... ELSE value END` checks its branches from top to bottom and uses the first one that matches.
Because the branches run in order, a later branch only needs the lower bound of its band.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: replace the fixed band with a CASE expression on price
SELECT id, name, price, 'cheap' AS band
FROM products
ORDER BY id;
sql.solution:
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  price,
  CASE
    WHEN price < 20 THEN 'cheap'
    WHEN price < 100 THEN 'standard'
    ELSE 'premium'
  END AS band
FROM products
ORDER BY id;
